definition: RAMnets is one of the oldest practical neurally inspired classification algorithms.
details: The RAMnets is also known as a type of "n-tuple recognition method" or "weightless neural network".

explainer.lead: RAMnets is one of the oldest practical neurally inspired classification algorithms. It matters as an early demonstration of classifying data without conventional weighted connections.

tiers.eli5: Instead of learning by slowly adjusting weights, RAMnets memorises patterns by looking at small groups of bits — like recognising someone by their hat plus their shoes rather than the whole face.
tiers.practitioner: Used as a lightweight classifier, RAMnets is also known as a type of n-tuple recognition method or weightless neural network. Its pitfall is limited flexibility relative to weight-based networks.
tiers.paperLevel: A neurally inspired classification algorithm known as a type of n-tuple recognition method, or weightless neural network.

explainer.example: A pattern-recognition task is split so that each n-tuple of input bits addresses a memory; the network classifies by tallying matches across many such tuples.
